verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents a built-in rate limiter with stricter default rules on auth paths (e.g. /sign-in/email limited to 3 requests per 10 seconds), configurable windows and IP-header handling, and a community user confirms rate limiting is built in. That directly covers brute-force throttling. Bot detection and IP blocking appear only as a one-line homepage claim with no docs or hands-on detail, and nothing specifically addresses credential stuffing. missing for 10: documented bot-detection/CAPTCHA mechanism, credential-stuffing-specific defenses (e.g. breached-password checks, account lockout), first-party docs for IP blocking, independent corroboration of bot protection.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can rely on built-in protection against bots, credential stuffing, and brute-force attacks on the auth flows

citations.quote: Better Auth includes a built-in rate limiter to help manage traffic and prevent abuse.
`/sign-in/email`: Is limited to 3 requests within 10 seconds.
Security & observability. Bot detection, IP blocking, and email validation.
things like email verification, password resets, and rate limiting come built-in or as simple plugins instead of having to code them myself.
